question: the two kb/markers copies carry different file sets

authority.evidence: mcp_server/eyekb_core.py line 21: EYEKB_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]          # /mnt/D/EyeKB -> line 23: KB = EYEKB_ROOT / "kb" -> line 213: MARKER_DIR = (KB / "markers"); no cross-tree fallback in either copy (searched both sources for a repo path or a fallback constant)
authority.second_evidence: the wave's own repository convention for this tree pair, as written in the repository-sync briefs that carry content the other way: 'copy, not move; the /mnt/D originals are not modified' — i.e. the data-volume tree is the origin and the git tree is the mirror

the_divergence_is_two_way.why_the_first_is_real: both files were created and committed in the git tree after the last content copy to the data volume, and the committed release's loader already names both of them in its own library map — so the git side is the newer authority here and the data tree is stale in the panel set, and its loader revision is older too
the_divergence_is_two_way.why_the_second_is_real: markers_v8_dev_retina.json has never been tracked in the git history (checked: git log --all over that path is empty), and markers_v9_dev_retina.json.v1 is a pre-revision copy; both are working files of the data tree that the release never carried

decision.what: no file is deleted and no existing file's bytes are touched. The two trees are made set-equal by copying the missing files in, byte-identically: the two increment panels the git tree carries into the data tree, and the dev panel the data tree carries can be mirrored into the git tree by a card that is allowed to move the release.
decision.why_not_done_in_this_card: this card's red lines forbid a kb/ body change and any activation, and the wave-2 gate that judges the marker layer rejects any kb/ file whose mtime is newer than that card's session start — a write here would leave an already-green gate red behind it. The reconciliation is therefore measured, decided and scripted, and the execution is left to a card that owns kb/ writes.
decision.execution: out/ITEM2_SYNC_KB_MARKERS.sh (dry run by default; --apply to execute)
decision.idempotent: yes: each copy is skipped when the destination already holds the same sha256, and no file is ever removed
